content: The South-East Asia Regional Immunization Technical Advisory Group (SEAR-ITAG) convened its seventh meeting, and the report was accessed on February 5, 2020. The meeting focused on progress in hepatitis B control and the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of the hepatitis B virus in the Western Pacific Region between 2005 and 2017, as documented in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) published in March 2019. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed guidelines for verifying the achievement of hepatitis B control targets through immunization in the South-East Asia Region. These guidelines, published in 2017, emphasize the importance of national and subnational vaccination coverage data, biomarker surveys, and other evidence to demonstrate progress toward elimination. The WHO also hosted a regional consultation on viral hepatitis in Europe in 2019, reaffirming countries' commitment to elimination goals. A framework for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B, and Chagas disease was published by the Pan American Health Organization in 2017. Additionally, WHO has provided best practices for conducting biomarker surveys to document the impact of hepatitis B immunization, including sample design and procedures, as outlined in a companion manual to the WHO cluster survey reference guide. The WHO has also issued consolidated strategic information guidelines for planning and tracking progress toward viral hepatitis elimination. These guidelines, updated in 2019, include recommendations for conducting serological surveys, ensuring data representativeness, and using appropriate testing methods. For example, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing is required for verification, and rapid tests with established sensitivity and specificity are acceptable for surveys. Ethical standards require that survey protocols be reviewed by an ethics committee before implementation, and surveys must comply with approved protocols. To verify hepatitis B control targets, countries must prepare a verification package that includes vaccination coverage data, biomarker survey reports, and other supporting evidence. This package should detail the objectives, methods, and results of serological surveys, including HBsAg prevalence and confidence intervals by age, gender, and other demographic factors. Countries should also address limitations in the data and provide plans for improving vaccination coverage in low-coverage areas. The verification process involves collaboration with the WHO Regional Office and a team of experts from the Verification Expert Panel (VEP). The panel reviews the submitted data and provides recommendations to the WHO Regional Director, who communicates the decision to the country. Sustainability of hepatitis B vaccination programs is critical. Countries are encouraged to develop plans to sustain or improve immunization coverage, including funding strategies and integration with national health plans. WHO provides technical support and resources to assist countries in achieving and maintaining hepatitis B control targets.
